qt: to the Commission Łukasz Kohut (S&D) Subject:

Are there currently plans to amend Regulation (EC) No 1082/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 July 2006 on a European grouping of territorial cooperation (EGTC) to allow entities not governed by public law to become members of an EGTC in order to allow private universities to join alliances that benefit from the EGTC’s legal status?
What is the Commission’s plan to finance alliances after the end of the current funding programme (Erasmus+)?
at: (English version) to the Commission Łukasz Kohut (S&D) (29 March 2024) Subject: European grouping of territorial cooperation and the funding of alliances 1. Are there currently plans to amend Regulation (EC) No 1082/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 July 2006 on a European grouping of territorial cooperation (EGTC) to allow entities not governed by public law to become members of an EGTC in order to allow private universities to join alliances that benefit from the EGTC’s legal status? 2.
What is the Commission’s plan to finance alliances after the end of the current funding programme (Erasmus+)?

(18 June 2024) Under the Erasmus+ programme (1), four projects under the 2022 European policy experimentation call in higher education (2) have been analysing the potential of existing European instruments to meet the needs of alliances of higher education institutions to pool some of their resources. Regulation (EC) No 1082/2006 on a European grouping of territorial cooperation (the EGTC regulation) (3) is one of the instruments that is being piloted. The Commission plans to publish a report on the final results of the Erasmus+ policy experimentation project s (4) by the end of 2024. The next steps will be then discussed in the European Council, building on the European degree packag e (5) adopted by the Commission on 27 March 2024. The Commission is working with the alliances, stakeholders and Member States on an investment pathway for alliances for the period 2028-2034 to support the long-term commitment of the European Universities initiative (6). The aim is to secure a more comprehensive funding approach, complementing the educational dimension with support across all alliances’ missions, looking for synergies between the different EU instruments as well as with national and regional sources of funding.
